observation.visible_scene: Low-angle close view of a car wheel (black Pirelli tire on a silver five-spoke alloy rim) on a gravel/asphalt surface, with a horizontal row of four individually clear-plastic-wrapped muffins laid on the ground along the tire's path. A white car body panel is partly visible at the top-left at the start.
visible_changes: The wheel translates leftward across the frame (the car moves left), so the white body panel slides out of view on the left and the tire's ground-contact point sweeps from the rightmost muffin toward the leftmost.

Each packaged muffin, initially upright and plump, is progressively squeezed into a thin flat disc as the tire rolls over it, in right-to-left order; the plastic film wrinkles and the paper cup spreads outward.
The rightmost muffin is already partly flattened at the first frame; by the last frame all four lie flattened in the same horizontal row.
The alloy rim's spokes rotate, showing the tire is rolling rather than simply sliding.
The muffins' horizontal positions stay roughly fixed throughout—they deform in place rather than being pushed along the ground.
Camera/background: the row of muffins holds nearly constant frame positions, indicating the camera is essentially stationary while the car/tire moves.
The four muffins remain as four separate packaged items in a line for the whole excerpt; no muffin is added, removed, or merged.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the car began moving and its speed (the rolling is already underway at frame 1).
Whether the tire entered from off-screen right before this crop, and what happens after the tire passes the leftmost muffin.
Whether the muffins were placed deliberately for this test.
The exact material/recipe of the baked goods.
uncertain_details: Any slight camera drift versus pure car translation is hard to confirm from the gravel texture, though the stable muffin positions suggest the camera is near-stationary.
Precise wheel rotation rate and the exact moment each muffin reaches full flattening.
Whether the items are muffins or similar packaged cakes (only appearance supports 'packaged baked goods').
